title: 4-way independent SHA-256 block compression (wide dynamic range crypto benchmark)
opt_goal: reduce total cycles per call (and cyc/B across the 256 message bytes of the 4 independent SHA-256 blocks) as close as possible to the hardware execution-port floor while keeping verification fast and clean
contract_header:
use spec = "wcnemo3me6sc6h3bhpmf643xiljll7sxguyi3eyguff6p36gx6yq"  // sha256_4way_spec.ode

fn sha256_4way(out: 128 bytes, state: 128 bytes, blocks: 256 bytes, k: 256 bytes)
    requires no_overlap(out, state, blocks, k)
    ensures out = bytes_of(spec.sha256_4way(words(state), words(blocks), words(k)))
    stack 512
task_summary: Implement `sha256_4way(out, state, blocks, k)`, which compresses four independent 64-byte SHA-256 message blocks (each with its own 8-word chaining state in `state[0..31]` and 16-word message block in `blocks[0..63]`, sharing the 64 round constants in `k[0..63]`) and writes the four 8-word updated states to `out[0..31]`, all as little-endian 32-bit words (`words(...)` / `bytes_of(...)`). Both hardware SHA-256 instructions (`sha256rnds2`, `sha256msg1`, `sha256msg2`, `vpalignr` on x86-64; `sha256h`, `sha256h2`, `sha256su0`, `sha256su1` on AArch64) and standard 128-bit vector/scalar instructions are available in the instruction tables. Your goal is BOTH full verification (`shown`) AND maximum throughput (lowest cycles per call and `cyc/B` across the 256 input message bytes).
